obstacle

/OB-stuh-kul/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Obstacle means something that blocks or hinders progress, movement, or achievement.

A rockslide left a pile of boulders across the mountain road — an obstacle no car could get past.

Example

The biggest obstacle to the vaccine campaign was distance: many villages lay a full day's walk from the nearest clinic.

Nothing physical is lying in the road here — distance itself is what blocks the goal. An obstacle can be any condition that stands between you and what you're trying to achieve, not just a physical object.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

hindrance: A hindrance makes progress harder without stopping it — an ongoing drag, like a slow laptop or a noisy office, that costs you speed for as long as it lasts. An obstacle blocks the path outright: progress waits until you deal with it. A hindrance slows the journey; an obstacle interrupts it.

impediment: An impediment delays or blocks movement, and the word leans formal and often built-in — a speech impediment, a legal impediment written into the contract. An obstacle usually sits in the path from outside: a boulder, a cost, a rival. Impediments tend to travel with you; obstacles stand in front of you.

hurdle: A hurdle is a difficulty you must get over to move forward, and the word promises it can be cleared — often one of a series, like the fences on a track. An obstacle makes no such promise: it simply blocks, and you may have to remove it, go around it, or give up.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

advantage: a condition that helps you succeed

boost: something that pushes progress forward

Where it sits · how completely progress is halted

snag → obstacle → impasse

snag vs. obstacle: A snag is a small hitch that slows you down for a moment; an obstacle genuinely blocks your path until you deal with it.

impasse vs. obstacle: An impasse is stronger than an obstacle — progress doesn't just get blocked, it stops completely, with no way forward in sight.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ob-: against, in the way (Latin)

Root — sta: to stand (Latin stare)

Suffix — -cle: a thing that (noun-forming ending)

Put it together: An obstacle is literally 'a thing that stands against you' — ob- (in the way) plus the Latin root stare (to stand): something standing squarely in your path.

Use the root in a new word: obstinate: Despite every counterargument, the committee chair remained obstinate about the deadline.

Root Check

Word Choice

Neutral

You overcome, remove, or face an obstacle, and something is an obstacle to a goal: 'an obstacle to peace,' 'an obstacle to progress.' It can be physical (a fallen tree) or abstract (fear, cost, distance) — and an obstacle course strings physical ones together on purpose.
